en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll tell stories like a confident B2 speaker: choosing each past tense on purpose, adding had been + -ing, and talking about old habits. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Three tenses, three jobs
steps.text: You already know these three past tenses. At B2, you choose each one on purpose.
steps.body:
**Past continuous** (was/were + -ing) = the scene: **in the middle** of something at that moment.
**Past simple** = the events, in order, or something that happened at that exact moment.
**Past perfect** (had + third form) = **already finished** before that moment.
The same verb tells three stories: the train **was leaving** (I saw it go), **left** (just as I arrived), **had left** (it was gone).
Indonesian trap: *sedang* and *sudah* are often dropped, but English must choose: *sudah* in a past story → **had** (*the film had already started*, not *already started*).

pairs.en: When I got to the platform, the train was leaving.
pairs.id: Waktu saya sampai di peron, keretanya sedang berangkat.

pairs.en: When I got to the platform, the train left.
pairs.id: Waktu saya sampai di peron, keretanya (langsung) berangkat.

pairs.en: When I got to the platform, the train had left.
pairs.id: Waktu saya sampai di peron, keretanya sudah berangkat.

pairs.en: It was raining, and people were pushing.
pairs.id: Hujan turun, dan orang-orang saling dorong. (latar)

pairs.en: I squeezed in and closed my eyes.
pairs.id: Saya menyelip masuk lalu memejamkan mata. (kejadian)

pairs.en: Suddenly I realised that I had left my laptop at the office.
pairs.id: Tiba-tiba saya sadar laptop saya tertinggal di kantor. (mundur)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi's morning, minute by minute.

question.prompt: Budi walked into the kitchen at 8:00. His wife started making coffee at 7:55 and finished at 8:05. Complete: When Budi walked into the kitchen, his wife ___ coffee.
options: made
was making
had made
question.explanation: At 8:00 she was **in the middle** of making coffee (7:55–8:05) → past continuous: **was making**. 'had made' would mean it was already finished before 8:00, and 'made' would mean she made it after he walked in.

steps.title: had been + -ing
steps.text: Now the new tense. It's the past version of I've been waiting.
steps.body:
**Past perfect continuous = had been + -ing**, the same for every person (short form **'d been**). Use it for an activity that went on **for a while up to a moment in the past**:
*I've been waiting for an hour* (up to now) → *I **had been waiting** for an hour **when** she called* (up to then).
It often comes with **for, since, all day, How long**.
Indonesian trap: *Saya sudah menunggu dua jam waktu dia datang* → not *I waited* or *I was waiting for two hours when she came*, but **I had been waiting for two hours when she came**.

pairs.en: had been waiting
pairs.id: sudah menunggu (sampai saat itu)

pairs.en: I've been waiting for an hour.
pairs.id: Saya sudah menunggu sejam. (sampai sekarang)

pairs.en: I had been waiting for an hour when she called.
pairs.id: Saya sudah menunggu sejam waktu dia menelepon. (sampai saat itu)

pairs.en: We'd been driving since 5 a.m.
pairs.id: Kami sudah menyetir sejak jam 5 pagi. ('d been = had been)

pairs.en: How long had you been living there?
pairs.id: Sudah berapa lama kamu tinggal di sana (waktu itu)?

steps.title: Up to a past moment
steps.text: Picture Rina at a café in Bandung. How long had she been waiting?

timeline.title: Rina had been waiting for two hours when Sari arrived.
timeline.caption: Rina started waiting at 5:00 and kept waiting up to 7:00, the moment Sari arrived → had been waiting (for two hours). Sari's arrival is the past moment → past simple: arrived.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas had a bad day in March.

question.prompt: Complete: Dimas failed his driving test in March, even though he ___ for it since January.
options: was practising
has been practising
had been practising
question.explanation: He practised from January **up to** the test in March, a past moment → **had been practising**. 'was practising' can't show how long (it doesn't go with since), and 'has been practising' means up to now. (American spelling: practicing.)

steps.title: had done or had been doing?
steps.text: The same choice as I've read vs I've been reading, now moved into the past.
steps.body:
**had been + -ing** = the **activity**: how long, or the reason for something you could **see** then: *The streets were wet. It **had been raining**.*
**had + third form** = the **result**, how many: *By noon she **had answered** 40 emails* (not *had been answering 40 emails*).
State verbs (know, like, have = own, be) stay simple: *I **had known** him for years* (not *had been knowing*).
With live, work, study + for/since, both forms are fine.

pairs.en: The streets were wet. It had been raining.
pairs.id: Jalanannya basah. Habis hujan.

pairs.en: Dimas was out of breath because he had been running.
pairs.id: Dimas terengah-engah karena habis lari.

pairs.en: By noon she had answered 40 emails.
pairs.id: Sampai jam 12 siang dia sudah membalas 40 email.

pairs.en: I had known him for ten years.
pairs.id: Saya sudah kenal dia selama sepuluh tahun.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: The kids come home after playing outside.

question.prompt: The kids came home with dirty clothes and muddy shoes. Arrange the words to say why (mereka habis main di lumpur).
question.solution: They had been playing in the mud.
question.explanation: The dirty clothes were the result you could see, and the playing had just stopped → **had been + -ing**: *They had been playing*, then where: *in the mud*.

steps.title: would and used to
steps.text: Last part: old habits, the way people tell memories.
steps.body:
**used to** + verb = past habits **and** states: *I used to have a bike. We used to live in Bogor.*
**would** + verb = only **repeated actions** in a memory story, after the time is set: *Every Sunday my dad **would take** me to the market.* Here would = *dulu biasanya*, not *akan*.
**Never would for states** (have, live, like, know, be): *I would have a bike* ✗ → **I used to have a bike** ✓.
One event → past simple. **'d** + base verb = would (*we'd play*).

pairs.en: I used to have a bike.
pairs.id: Dulu saya punya sepeda. (keadaan)

pairs.en: We used to live in Bogor.
pairs.id: Dulu kami tinggal di Bogor. (keadaan)

pairs.en: Every Sunday my dad would take me to the market.
pairs.id: Setiap Minggu ayah dulu biasa mengajak saya ke pasar. (kegiatan berulang)

pairs.en: After school, we'd play football until it got dark.
pairs.id: Sepulang sekolah, kami dulu biasa main bola sampai gelap.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Bu Ani tells you about growing up in Solo.

question.prompt: Bu Ani is remembering her childhood in Solo. Which sentence is wrong?
options: My grandfather used to have a big garden.
My grandfather would have a big garden.
Every Friday we would eat at the night market.
question.explanation: have a garden = own it, a **state** → would is impossible here: **used to have** (or *had*). 'Every Friday we would eat …' is a repeated action with the time set first, so would is fine.

steps.title: Back to the story
steps.text: One last choice of tense, at the office.

question.prompt: Rina was late for the team meeting. Which sentence means she missed ALL of Pak Hasan's presentation?
options: When Rina came in, Pak Hasan had given his presentation.
When Rina came in, Pak Hasan was giving his presentation.
When Rina came in, Pak Hasan gave his presentation.
question.explanation: **had given** = the presentation was already finished before she came in, so she missed all of it. 'was giving' = he was in the middle of it (she missed only the start), and 'gave' = he gave it at the moment she came in or right after.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for your next story.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · narrative tenses
artifact.intro: Every verb in a story has a job. Choose the tense that does that job.
rows: was/were + -ing
the scene: in the middle at that moment
It was raining, and people were pushing.
past simple
the events, in order
I squeezed in and closed my eyes.
had + third form
already finished before that moment
I realised I had left my laptop at the office.
had been + -ing
going on for a while up to a past moment
I had been waiting for two hours when she arrived.
had been + -ing
the reason for something you could see
The streets were wet. It had been raining.
had + third form
a number or a finished result
By noon she had answered 40 emails.
used to + verb
past habits AND states
I used to have a bike.
would + verb
repeated actions only, after the time is set
Every Sunday my dad would take me to the market.
tips: **sudah** in a past story → **had**; a wait or activity **up to** a past moment → **had been + -ing**, not *I waited for two hours when …*
Counting finished things (40 emails) → had + third form. State verbs (know, have, like, be) → never had been + -ing.
**would** for old habits: actions only. *I would have a bike* ✗ → *I used to have a bike* ✓.

examples.en: When I got to the platform, the train had left.
examples.id: Waktu saya sampai di peron, keretanya sudah berangkat.

examples.en: We'd been driving since 5 a.m., so we stopped at a rest area.
examples.id: Kami sudah menyetir sejak jam 5 pagi, jadi kami berhenti di rest area.

examples.en: We used to live in a small house near the rice fields.
examples.id: Dulu kami tinggal di rumah kecil dekat sawah.

examples.en: Every evening, my grandmother would tell us stories.
examples.id: Setiap malam, nenek dulu biasa mendongeng untuk kami.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar bercerita seperti pembicara B2 yang percaya diri: memilih setiap past tense dengan sengaja, menambahkan had been + -ing, dan bercerita tentang kebiasaan lama. Ayo kita mulai pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Tiga tense, tiga tugas
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal ketiga past tense ini. Di B2, kamu memilih masing-masing dengan sengaja.
steps.body:
**Past continuous** (was/were + -ing) = latarnya: sesuatu yang **sedang berlangsung** pada saat itu.
**Past simple** = kejadian-kejadiannya, sesuai urutan, atau sesuatu yang terjadi tepat pada saat itu.
**Past perfect** (had + bentuk ketiga) = **sudah selesai** sebelum saat itu.
Kata kerja yang sama menceritakan tiga hal: the train **was leaving** (saya melihatnya pergi), **left** (persis waktu saya sampai), **had left** (keretanya sudah tidak ada).
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *sedang* dan *sudah* sering tidak diucapkan, tapi bahasa Inggris harus memilih: *sudah* dalam cerita lampau → **had** (*the film had already started*, bukan *already started*).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pagi Budi, menit demi menit.

question.prompt: Budi masuk ke dapur jam 8.00. Istrinya mulai membuat kopi jam 7.55 dan selesai jam 8.05. Lengkapi: When Budi walked into the kitchen, his wife ___ coffee.
options: made
was making
had made
question.explanation: Jam 8.00 istrinya **sedang** membuat kopi (7.55–8.05) → past continuous: **was making**. 'had made' berarti kopinya sudah selesai sebelum jam 8.00, dan 'made' berarti dia membuatnya setelah Budi masuk.

steps.title: had been + -ing
steps.text: Sekarang tense yang baru. Ini versi lampau dari I've been waiting.
steps.body:
**Past perfect continuous = had been + -ing**, sama untuk semua orang (bentuk pendek **'d been**). Pakai untuk kegiatan yang sudah berlangsung **beberapa lama sampai suatu saat di masa lalu**:
*I've been waiting for an hour* (sampai sekarang) → *I **had been waiting** for an hour **when** she called* (sampai saat itu).
Sering muncul dengan **for, since, all day, How long**.
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Saya sudah menunggu dua jam waktu dia datang* → bukan *I waited* atau *I was waiting for two hours when she came*, tapi **I had been waiting for two hours when she came**.

pairs.id: sudah menunggu (sampai saat itu)

pairs.en: I've been waiting for an hour.
pairs.id: Saya sudah menunggu sejam. (sampai sekarang)

pairs.en: I had been waiting for an hour when she called.
pairs.id: Saya sudah menunggu sejam waktu dia menelepon. (sampai saat itu)

pairs.en: We'd been driving since 5 a.m.
pairs.id: Kami sudah menyetir sejak jam 5 pagi. ('d been = had been)

pairs.en: How long had you been living there?
pairs.id: Sudah berapa lama kamu tinggal di sana (waktu itu)?

steps.title: Sampai suatu saat di masa lalu
steps.text: Bayangkan Rina di sebuah kafe di Bandung. Sudah berapa lama dia menunggu?

timeline.title: Rina had been waiting for two hours when Sari arrived.
timeline.caption: Rina mulai menunggu jam 5.00 dan terus menunggu sampai jam 7.00, saat Sari datang → had been waiting (for two hours). Datangnya Sari adalah saat di masa lalu itu → past simple: arrived.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas mengalami hari yang buruk di bulan Maret.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas failed his driving test in March, even though he ___ for it since January.
options: was practising
has been practising
had been practising
question.explanation: Dia berlatih dari Januari **sampai** ujiannya di bulan Maret, suatu saat di masa lalu → **had been practising**. 'was practising' tidak bisa menunjukkan berapa lama (tidak cocok dengan since), dan 'has been practising' berarti sampai sekarang. (Ejaan Amerika: practicing.)

steps.title: had done atau had been doing?
steps.text: Pilihan yang sama seperti I've read dan I've been reading, sekarang dipindah ke masa lalu.
steps.body:
**had been + -ing** = **kegiatannya**: berapa lama, atau alasan untuk sesuatu yang **terlihat** saat itu: *The streets were wet. It **had been raining**.*
**had + bentuk ketiga** = **hasilnya**, berapa banyak: *By noon she **had answered** 40 emails* (bukan *had been answering 40 emails*).
Kata kerja keadaan (know, like, have = punya, be) tetap simple: *I **had known** him for years* (bukan *had been knowing*).
Dengan live, work, study + for/since, kedua bentuk benar.

pairs.en: The streets were wet. It had been raining.
pairs.id: Jalanannya basah. Habis hujan.

pairs.en: Dimas was out of breath because he had been running.
pairs.id: Dimas terengah-engah karena habis lari.

pairs.en: By noon she had answered 40 emails.
pairs.id: Sampai jam 12 siang dia sudah membalas 40 email.

pairs.en: I had known him for ten years.
pairs.id: Saya sudah kenal dia selama sepuluh tahun.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Anak-anak pulang setelah main di luar.

question.prompt: Anak-anak pulang dengan baju kotor dan sepatu penuh lumpur. Susun kata-katanya untuk menjelaskan alasannya (mereka habis main di lumpur).
question.solution: They had been playing in the mud.
question.explanation: Baju kotor adalah hasil yang terlihat, dan mainnya baru saja berhenti → **had been + -ing**: *They had been playing*, lalu di mana: *in the mud*.

steps.title: would dan used to
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: kebiasaan lama, seperti orang bercerita tentang kenangan.
steps.body:
**used to** + kata kerja = kebiasaan **dan** keadaan lampau: *I used to have a bike. We used to live in Bogor.*
**would** + kata kerja = hanya **kegiatan yang berulang** dalam cerita kenangan, setelah waktunya disebut: *Every Sunday my dad **would take** me to the market.* Di sini would = *dulu biasanya*, bukan *akan*.
**Jangan pakai would untuk keadaan** (have, live, like, know, be): *I would have a bike* ✗ → **I used to have a bike** ✓.
Satu kejadian → past simple. **'d** + kata kerja dasar = would (*we'd play*).

pairs.en: I used to have a bike.
pairs.id: Dulu saya punya sepeda. (keadaan)

pairs.en: We used to live in Bogor.
pairs.id: Dulu kami tinggal di Bogor. (keadaan)

pairs.en: Every Sunday my dad would take me to the market.
pairs.id: Setiap Minggu ayah dulu biasa mengajak saya ke pasar. (kegiatan berulang)

pairs.en: After school, we'd play football until it got dark.
pairs.id: Sepulang sekolah, kami dulu biasa main bola sampai gelap.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bu Ani bercerita tentang masa kecilnya di Solo.

question.prompt: Bu Ani sedang mengenang masa kecilnya di Solo. Kalimat mana yang salah?
options: My grandfather used to have a big garden.
My grandfather would have a big garden.
Every Friday we would eat at the night market.
question.explanation: have a garden = punya kebun, sebuah **keadaan** → would tidak bisa dipakai di sini: **used to have** (atau *had*). 'Every Friday we would eat …' adalah kegiatan berulang dan waktunya sudah disebut dulu, jadi would boleh.

steps.title: Kembali ke cerita
steps.text: Satu pilihan tense terakhir, di kantor.

question.prompt: Rina terlambat datang ke rapat tim. Kalimat mana yang berarti dia ketinggalan SELURUH presentasi Pak Hasan?
options: When Rina came in, Pak Hasan had given his presentation.
When Rina came in, Pak Hasan was giving his presentation.
When Rina came in, Pak Hasan gave his presentation.
question.explanation: **had given** = presentasinya sudah selesai sebelum Rina masuk, jadi dia ketinggalan semuanya. 'was giving' = Pak Hasan sedang presentasi (Rina hanya ketinggalan awalnya), dan 'gave' = dia presentasi tepat saat Rina masuk atau sesudahnya.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajarannya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk ceritamu berikutnya.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · narrative tenses
artifact.intro: Setiap kata kerja dalam cerita punya tugas. Pilih tense yang menjalankan tugas itu.
rows: was/were + -ing
latar: sedang berlangsung saat itu
It was raining, and people were pushing.
past simple
kejadian-kejadiannya, sesuai urutan
I squeezed in and closed my eyes.
had + bentuk ketiga
sudah selesai sebelum saat itu
I realised I had left my laptop at the office.
had been + -ing
berlangsung beberapa lama sampai suatu saat di masa lalu
I had been waiting for two hours when she arrived.
had been + -ing
alasan untuk sesuatu yang terlihat
The streets were wet. It had been raining.
had + bentuk ketiga
jumlah atau hasil yang sudah selesai
By noon she had answered 40 emails.
used to + kata kerja
kebiasaan DAN keadaan lampau
I used to have a bike.
would + kata kerja
hanya kegiatan berulang, setelah waktunya disebut
Every Sunday my dad would take me to the market.
tips: **sudah** dalam cerita lampau → **had**; menunggu atau kegiatan **sampai** suatu saat di masa lalu → **had been + -ing**, bukan *I waited for two hours when …*
Menghitung hal yang sudah selesai (40 email) → had + bentuk ketiga. Kata kerja keadaan (know, have, like, be) → tidak pernah had been + -ing.
**would** untuk kebiasaan lama: hanya kegiatan. *I would have a bike* ✗ → *I used to have a bike* ✓.
